title: A Cellar for the Smile
premise: Folklorist Emrys Dunmore returns to the village of Hollowmere to record its dying songs, only to find every photograph from their grandmother's house now shows an extra chair—and the villagers refuse to sing any song twice, as if repetition is an invitation. Digging into their grandmother's ledgers, Emrys learns she once bargained with something beneath the cellar to spare the village a killing frost, a debt renewed each generation by an heir who must 'hold out until sunrise' in that house. When the villagers mark Emrys as the current heir and seal them inside, they must piece together the truth of what was invited in before the frost completes its final windowpane pattern at dawn. Emrys survives by refusing both denial and obedience—singing the forbidden song back to the thing below, naming it, and breaking the inheritance—but only at the cost of the village's memory of their grandmother, whom no one but Emrys will ever remember again.
about_author: Beatrix Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories in remote farming communities before turning to fiction. They write horror about the debts families hide in plain sight, and claim to have never recorded the same song twice.

chapters.title: The Songs They Won't Repeat
chapters.summary: Emrys arrives in Hollowmere with recording equipment and academic skepticism. A pub singer cuts off mid-verse when Emrys asks him to sing it again, going pale and leaving. POV: Emrys. Beat: curiosity sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: Grandmother's House, Still Standing
chapters.summary: Emrys inherits and moves into the late Maren Dunmore's house on the village edge. Neighbors are warm but oddly formal, calling them 'the heir' before Emrys mentions any inheritance. POV: Emrys. Beat: belonging laced with dread.

chapters.title: An Extra Chair
chapters.summary: Sorting photographs, Emrys notices every image—from 1962 to last spring—now includes a plain wooden chair against the wall that wasn't there before. The chair appears even in photos taken outdoors. POV: Emrys. Beat: rational explanations begin to fail.

chapters.title: What the Frost Draws
chapters.summary: A cold snap in early autumn. Frost patterns on the windows form deliberate shapes: a doorway, a staircase descending. Emrys photographs them; the photos show only the chair. POV: Emrys. Beat: isolation deepens as evidence refuses to travel.

chapters.title: The Verse That Isn't Sung
chapters.summary: At the harvest gathering, an old woman begins a lullaby and the whole room goes silent at verse four. Emrys records it covertly; playback reveals a second voice beneath the melody. POV: Emrys. Beat: first hard proof, and terror with it.

chapters.title: Maren's Ledgers
chapters.summary: In the cellar office, Emrys finds grandmother's meticulous accounts—not money, but dates, names, and one recurring entry: 'held until sunrise. Paid.' The final page names Emrys. POV: Emrys. Beat: the personal stakes become undeniable.

chapters.title: The Village Remembers Differently
chapters.summary: Emrys questions neighbors about Maren. Each gives a different account of her death—one says winter, one says spring, one says 'she never left.' Their stories rearrange slightly between tellings. POV: Emrys. Beat: reality's seams showing.

chapters.title: Down the Cellar Stairs
chapters.summary: Compelled by a sound like humming, Emrys descends to the cellar and finds the extra chair from the photographs, real, facing a bricked-up alcove. The brick is warm. POV: Emrys. Beat: confrontation with the physical presence.

chapters.title: I Don't Believe
chapters.summary: Emrys flees to the village inn, reciting skepticism like a prayer. But the innkeeper's child draws a picture of Emrys sitting in a chair, smiling, and the drawing chills everyone who sees it. POV: Emrys. Beat: denial curdling into complicity-fear.

chapters.title: The Debt Explained
chapters.summary: The old woman from the gathering visits and tells the truth obliquely: generations ago, the Dunmores invited something in to end a killing frost, and each heir must sit in the chair until sunrise once per lifetime. Maren did it for forty years. POV: mostly the old woman, framed by Emrys. Beat: the rules made explicit.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Emrys decides to leave instead. Packing the car at night, they find the road loops back to Hollowmere no matter which direction they drive. The frost patterns now spell their name. POV: Emrys. Beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: Marked
chapters.summary: Villagers stop meeting Emrys's eyes. Doors close. Someone nails a sprig of rowan to Emrys's gate—protection for the village, not the guest. Emrys realizes they've been cast as the sacrifice. POV: Emrys. Beat: betrayal and rage.

chapters.title: Maren's Last Recording
chapters.summary: Among the ledgers, a reel-to-reel tape: Maren's voice singing the forbidden fourth verse alone, then speaking directly to her future heir: 'Don't sit. Sing. It hates being named.' The tape degrades as it plays. POV: Emrys. Beat: inheritance reframed as weapon.

chapters.title: The First Night
chapters.summary: Frost seals the doors and windows from outside. The cellar door stands open though Emrys locked it. All night, the humming climbs the stairs, patient, stopping just short of the bedroom. POV: Emrys. Beat: siege begins.

chapters.title: The Smile
chapters.summary: Emrys catches their reflection wearing a smile they aren't making. In photos taken that morning, they are already seated in the chair. Time is being edited around them. POV: Emrys. Beat: identity under assault—the horror of becoming the photograph.

chapters.title: Allies at the Edge
chapters.summary: The old woman and the innkeeper's child sneak supplies through the frost line. The woman admits the village let Maren carry the debt alone out of cowardice, and gives Emrys the song's true name, half-erased. POV: alternating Emrys and the old woman. Beat: solidarity kindled in guilt.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: Researching parish records, Emrys reconstructs the original bargain: during the Year Without a Summer, the first Dunmore sang something up from under the land and promised it warmth, company, and heirs. It isn't evil—it is kept, like a guest who was never allowed to leave. POV: Emrys. Beat: pity complicates fear.

chapters.title: The Second Night
chapters.summary: The frost writes a complete doorway on the kitchen window. The chair drags itself upstairs. Emrys, exhausted, nearly sits—catches themselves mid-descent, hands on the seat, smiling. POV: Emrys. Beat: climax approach; will at its thinnest.

chapters.title: Sunrise Vigil
chapters.summary: Emrys carries the chair to the cellar, sits facing the alcove—not surrender, but positioning—and begins the forbidden verse, inserting the creature's true name where the erased syllable belongs. The brick cracks. Dawn light enters with them. POV: Emrys. Beat: climax.

chapters.title: Naming
chapters.summary: Face to face with what the family kept—a gaunt figure of rime and patience—Emrys finishes the song and speaks its name aloud, ending the bargain: not banishing it, but releasing it. The frost patterns melt into ordinary water. The chair crumbles to ash. POV: Emrys. Beat: catharsis through compassion rather than violence.

chapters.title: The Price of Memory
chapters.summary: Aftermath: the village is safe but Maren has vanished from every ledger, gravestone, and mind except Emrys's. Even the old woman stares blankly at the name. Emrys alone carries the inheritance now—not the debt, but the remembering. POV: Emrys. Beat: grief and bitter triumph.

chapters.title: One Song, Sung Twice
chapters.summary: Spring. Emrys stays in Hollowmere as its unofficial archivist. At the pub, they ask the singer to perform the lullaby again—and he does, all four verses, weeping without knowing why. Outside, the windows stay clear. POV: Emrys. Beat: resolution; memory reclaimed, fear unlearned.
